findings.title: Learning companionship has a patience contract
findings.claim: The focus condition makes the learning companionship a bounded relation: a further question ends the shared accompaniment, while explanation remains possible after the separation.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms for questioning and sustained companionship meet the earlier patience warning and no-question condition; the later separation and return to outcome make the relational boundary concrete.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the threatened loss is relational as well as intellectual: the learner may still receive an explanation, but no longer from inside the shared journey that made the instruction possible.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains Moses's self-imposed condition and acknowledgement of an excuse. This finding does not turn the pericope into a general theory of teaching or claim that separation cancels the later explanation.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel supports directly supply the patience limit, question breach, companionship boundary, separation, and later interpretation contacts.

findings.title: Reaching marks a sequence of thresholds

findings.mechanism: The focus reaching form meets arrival at 18:60 and 18:61, the gathered meeting-point carrier, the later parting, and the orphans' reaching full strength. These contacts turn the focus excuse into a relational endpoint within a journey of arrivals rather than a detached reason for leaving.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the focus sentence as an arrival at a limit, while the later maturity scene keeps an endpoint from being forced before its time.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that the addressee has supplied a sufficient excuse. The HFT roles are legacy_unbound and unresolved records remain attributed; no lexicon gloss or facet is invented for those records.

findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains the conditional warning that another question ends companionship. This finding does not condemn inquiry in general or claim that the learner has no knowledge at all.

findings.title: The excuse becomes a waiver
findings.claim: After the earlier plea against accountability and the repeated failure of patience, the focus excuse can be read as granting the guide release from any obligation to continue the companionship.
findings.mechanism: The focus excuse and companionship forms meet the earlier request not to be held for forgetfulness, the repeated patience reminder, and the focus's conditional end of accompaniment. The same excuse word therefore changes sides: it is no longer another defense for the speaker but grounds the guide's release.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the final clause as a transfer of standing: the speaker concedes that the guide has already been given sufficient reason to end the relation.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains an apology or acknowledgement that the guide has an excuse. The HFT inference does not assert a technical legal transfer beyond this pericope or erase the speaker's remorse.

findings.mechanism: The focus companionship and question forms meet the third visible objection, the later separation form, and the report and outcome forms that follow it. The contact makes parting a pedagogical phase transition rather than a cancellation of instruction.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see that the loss of company and the arrival of explanation belong to one turn: shared travel ends, but the promised account begins from the other side of that boundary.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that another question ends the companionship. The finding does not claim that separation is only pedagogical or that later interpretation restores the lost shared journey.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies complete focus and pericope anchors, but its legacy_unbound provenance requires unresolved branch roles to remain attributed.

findings.containment: This is a form-distant exploratory analogy, not the ordinary lexical gloss of asking. The focus still says that another question ends companionship, and the analogy does not claim literal physical extraction or replace the plain reading.
